Local projections with joint cross-horizon covariance

Source: R/lp-joint.R
lp_joint.Rd

Same regressions as lp() but additionally returns, for every response, the covariance matrix of the whole impulse-response vector \((\hat\beta_0,\dots,\hat\beta_H)'\), $$\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}(\hat\beta_h,\hat\beta_{h'}) = \sum_{l=-L}^{L} w_l \sum_t q_{t,h} e_{t+h}\, q_{t-l,h'} e_{t-l+h'},\quad q_{t,h} = x_{t,h}'(X_h'X_h)^{-1}e_1,$$ with Bartlett weights \(w_l = 1-|l|/(L+1)\) and \(L = \max(h,h')+1\) (or a common nw_lag). The diagonal reproduces the standard errors of lp(). The engine is cpp_lp_cov (C++).

Usage

lp_joint(
  Y,
  shock,
  horizon = 20L,
  lags = 4L,
  contemp = NULL,
  controls = NULL,
  iv = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  cumulative = NULL,
  se = c("nw", "hc"),
  nw_lag = NULL,
  lag_augment = FALSE,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  dof_adjust = FALSE
)

Arguments

Y

data frame / tibble / matrix (T x K) of responses (and the source of lag controls). Non-numeric columns (e.g. a date) are dropped.

shock

the shock \(s_t\): a variable of Y (tidyselect; observed shock, unit-impact normalisation) or a numeric vector of length T (external shock series, e.g. narrative).

horizon

maximum horizon H.

lags

number of lags of Y in the controls (and of an external shock).

contemp

<tidy-select> variables of Y entered contemporaneously as controls. For a recursive (Cholesky) identification with shock a variable of Y, list the variables ordered before the shock.

controls

optional extra T x q matrix of controls.

iv

optional T x q matrix of instruments for shock (LP-IV; Stock & Watson 2018).

responses

<tidy-select> responses to use (default all variables of Y).

cumulative

<tidy-select> variables whose response is cumulated (\(\sum_{j=0}^h y_{t+j}\)), for variables measured in differences.

se

"nw" Newey-West/Bartlett or "hc" Eicker-Huber-White (HC1).

nw_lag

Newey-West truncation lag; default h + 1.

lag_augment

Montiel Olea & Plagborg-Moller (2021) lag augmentation: add one extra lag that is not interpreted and use "hc" standard errors, valid without stationarity assumptions and robust at long horizons.

level

confidence levels for the pointwise bands.

dof_adjust

apply an n/(n-m) small-sample factor to the Newey-West variance.

Value

an lp_joint object (also an lpm) with the extra element $vcov: a named list (one per response) of \((H+1)\times(H+1)\) covariance matrices.

Details

Economic intuition. Local-projection estimates at neighbouring horizons are built from overlapping data and highly correlated, so reading a pointwise band as a statement about the whole response path overstates what the data say. The joint covariance is the input for simultaneous inference (lp_supt()), joint hypothesis tests (e.g. "the response is zero at all horizons"), and smoothing. Pitfall: with the default horizon-specific bandwidth the full matrix is not guaranteed positive semi-definite; use a common nw_lag if you need to invert it.

See also

Other local projections: autoplot.lpm(), compare_lp_var(), lp(), lp_forecast(), lp_panel(), lp_smooth(), lp_state(), lp_supt(), tidy.lpm()

Examples

fit <- lp_joint(yraw, shock = rate, horizon = 8, lags = 2, contemp = c(infl, unemp))
sqrt(diag(fit$vcov[[1]])) - fit$se[, 1] # zero
#>             0             1             2             3             4 
#> -2.524355e-29  2.775558e-17  1.387779e-17  4.163336e-17  5.551115e-17 
#>             5             6             7             8 
#>  2.775558e-17  2.775558e-17  0.000000e+00  0.000000e+00
